newsitem.title: MEXICO: One dead, 17 hurt in Mexican religious clash.
newsitem.headline: One dead, 17 hurt in Mexican religious clash.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1996-11-25

text.p: Mexicans of different religions and opposing political parties battled with rocks, hoes, machetes, axes and firearms, killing one person and injuring 17, authorities said on Monday.

"The confrontation (Sunday) was due to agrarian, political and religious causes that in recent months have worsened conflicts between Catholics and Evangelicals who belong to different parties," David Gomez, a state official who oversees Indian rights, told Reuters.

The clash among Tzeltal Maya Indians took place in the rural southeastern state of Chiapas, pitting Roman Catholics of the leftist opposition Democratic Revolution Party (PRD) against Protestant Evangelicals of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), Gomez said.
The state Attorney General's Office said in a statement it was investigating the incident and would bring murder charges in the shooting death of Pedro Aguilar of the PRD.

The Evangelicals of the ruling party were given land in the municipality of Venustiano Carranza by the government three months ago, but the Catholics of the opposition party considered the property theirs.

About 200 Catholics marched on the site on Sunday to measure the property, provoking the Evangelicals, who felt their homes were being intruded on, officials said. Soon the groups were fighting with everything from rocks to firearms.
Abdias Tovilla, a legal adviser for the Evangelical Defence Committee in Chiapas, told Reuters "a horrible shootout" began with the Catholics "threatening to expel the Evangelicals from their land."
Tovilla said friction worsened recently after the government began helping the Evangelicals build decent homes as the opposition Catholics continued to live in misery.
"After tearing down the posts that divide the territory, (the Catholics) began to argue and scream, leading to blows that set off the armed conflict," Tovilla said.
Some witnesses told Reuters police at the scene did nothing to intervene until other officers arrived several hours later.
